title: CmdPal: App is not being properly disposed

judgment.rationale: The issue identifies an asynchronous shutdown call followed by immediate process termination; ownership and disposal paths are visible in source.
evidence: MainWindow_Closed calls SignalStopAsync without awaiting it.
App owns the service provider and has a Dispose path that is bypassed.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve the App-owned bounded shutdown design.

fix_assessment.rationale: No existing fix attempt fully coordinates extension stop, service-provider disposal, and process exit.

proposed_fixes.title: Move CmdPal shutdown orchestration to App
proposed_fixes.root_cause: MainWindow starts asynchronous service shutdown but immediately calls Environment.Exit, so extension stop tasks and IDisposable DI singletons may never complete.
plan: Add an idempotent App-owned shutdown coordinator.
Let MainWindow perform UI-thread cleanup and request shutdown rather than exiting directly.
Await extension stops with a bounded timeout, dispose the provider once, then exit.
verification: Delayed fake services complete or time out before the process exits and service disposal occurs once for window, tray, and native exit paths.

confidence.rationale: The asynchronous call, immediate exit, App disposal path, and service registrations are directly confirmed.

issue_context.summary: CmdPal terminates from MainWindow before asynchronous extension shutdown and DI disposal can finish.
known_information: The issue points to MainWindow_Closed and Environment.Exit.
inferences: Shutdown ownership belongs at App/process scope rather than a window.
A bounded wait is needed to avoid hanging on a broken extension.
issue_context.analysis: Keeping UI cleanup on the UI thread and moving process exit after bounded asynchronous shutdown addresses both missed signals and skipped container disposal while preserving the existing explicit-exit workaround.
initial_investigation: Inspected MainWindow.xaml.cs, App.xaml.cs, IExtensionService, WinRTExtensionService, and ExtensionWrapper.
Reviewed local history containing a partial ProcessShutdownCoordinator pattern.
Fork mirror Issue 642 contains the detailed design and adversary conditions.

design.root_cause: MainWindow_Closed invokes SignalStopAsync as fire-and-forget and then calls Environment.Exit(0). Pending extension cleanup and App/service-provider disposal are therefore not guaranteed.
evidence: [Observed] App.Dispose disposes Services but is not called by the direct exit path.
[Inferred] A single idempotent process coordinator can unify all exit sources.

affected_files.purpose: Performs window-affine cleanup and currently owns direct exit.
Owns service provider and process lifetime.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: App constructs services and can dispose them, but the normal close path bypasses that disposal.
implementation_steps.change: Expose an idempotent process shutdown request that gathers service stop operations, waits with a bounded timeout, disposes the provider once, then exits.
edge_cases: Log individual stop failures and continue.
Do not block the UI thread.
Capture service delegates before provider disposal.
Reuse the path for native and tray exits.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The handler stops services without awaiting and exits immediately.
implementation_steps.change: Retain tray, hook, acrylic, and placement cleanup, then call App.Current.RequestProcessExit.
edge_cases: All UI-affine cleanup remains on the UI thread.
Repeated close events must be harmless.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: No coverage proves shutdown completion before exit.
implementation_steps.change: Test reentrancy, delayed services, timeout, failures, and exactly-once disposal.
edge_cases: A stop failure must not prevent disposal or exit.
A timeout must still invoke the exit callback.

verify: Build CmdPal UI and unit tests with the existing tools\build\build.cmd workflow.
Run targeted tests with vstest.console.exe after locating the produced test DLL.
Close via window, tray, and native exit paths; verify stop operations complete or time out before exit and disposal occurs once.
Verify tray removal, keyboard unhooking, acrylic cleanup, and window placement remain intact.
risks: A bounded wait can lengthen shutdown; the timeout prevents hangs.
Provider disposal may expose latent ordering defects, which tests should surface.
alternatives: Removing Environment.Exit changes an existing crash workaround.
Keeping shutdown in MainWindow cannot correctly cover process-wide exit sources.

mirror.fork_title: [Issue 50349] CmdPal App is not being properly disposed

adversary.verdict: No blocking objections if shutdown ownership is App-level, bounded, and idempotent.
adversary.notes: A fire-and-forget call in MainWindow remains unacceptable.

comment.body: Approve the fork-side App-owned shutdown design for Issue 50349.
